requirements.requirement: Run the inventory web application on node2, listening on port 8080.
requirements.summary: node2 served the inventory application from 0.0.0.0:8080, was reachable from node1, and remained enabled, active, firewall-accessible, and functional after restart.

requirements.requirement: Run the inventory web application on node3, listening on port 8080.
requirements.summary: node3 served the inventory application from 0.0.0.0:8080, was reachable from node1, and remained enabled, active, firewall-accessible, and functional after restart.

requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to accept HTTP on port 80 and load-balance requests across node2 and node3.
requirements.summary: node1 listened on 0.0.0.0:80 with HTTP allowed, and repeated requests alternated between node2 and node3. After node1 and backend restarts, final requests again alternated across both backends.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The mandatory restart protocol was completed on every node: each had a healthy pre-restart state, restart scheduling and disconnection, a changed boot identity matching the lifecycle cross-check, and recovered service and application behavior. Final load-balancer requests reached both recovered backends.
limitations: HTTP behavior was probed from within the managed topology rather than from an independent external client; listening addresses and firewall queries support, but do not independently demonstrate, off-topology reachability.
The environment has no formal cluster subsystem, so recovered integration state was demonstrated through successful load-balanced traffic rather than a separate cluster-status command.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear task or mandatory restart-evidence purposes: application deployment, service enablement, required firewall access, load-balancer deployment, and sequential restart verification. No unrelated troubleshooting mutation, failed service, or package damage is evident. The minor hygiene defect is retained transient evidence residue: node1 kept /tmp/inventory-response, /tmp/h, and /tmp/b, while all nodes kept /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log. These files remained after completion rather than being cleaned up, but are bounded and low risk.
